name: Satinder Kaur Brar
title: Professor and James and Joanne Love Chair in Environmental Engineering @ York University
bio:
Dr. Brar, the James and Joanne Love Chair in Environmental Engineering and Director of the One WATER Institute at York University, is an internationally acclaimed researcher with an H-index of 90. Her groundbreaking work bridges waste valorization and the removal of emerging contaminants, with applications of her biopesticide and biofertilizer technologies now implemented across several countries, including Vietnam, Morocco, and India. Ranked among the world's top 2% scientists by Stanford University (2021-2025), she has attracted over $25 million in research funding and leads the Inzymes Group at York.
Her career includes over 450 publications, 9 patents, and 18 books. She is a Fellow of the Canadian Academy of Engineering, the European Academy of Science and Arts, and the Royal Society of Canada. Recipient of numerous national and international awards, Dr. Brar's research has informed global policy and advanced sustainable solutions for water and environmental management.

name: Sandra Juutilainen
title: Assistant Professor, Indigenous Health and Nutrition @ Toronto Metropolitan University
bio: Dr. Juutilainen is Haudenosaunee (Oneida of the Thames) and Finnish-Canadian. She completed an undergraduate degree in Food and Nutrition at Toronto Metropolitan University (formerly Ryerson Polytechnic University), and the Yukon First Nations Dietetic Internship program. After working for 10 years as a registered dietitian in First Nations communities throughout Ontario and Yukon she moved to Finland to complete a Master of Health Science in Circumpolar Health and PhD in Health Sciences at the University of Oulu. She is currently a faculty member at Toronto Metropolitan University where she teaches in the School of Nutrition's undergraduate program. Sandra also holds an adjunct assistant professor appointment at the University of Waterloo in the School of Public Health Sciences. She is a member of the College of Dietitians of Ontario and Dietitians of Canada. Her research interests include: Indigenous health and wellness, human rights, critical dietetics, nutrition, food security, Indigenous food sovereignty, qualitative and mixed-methods research; and, community-driven research informed by Indigenous methodologies. In 2024, she was awarded The Dean's Scholarly, Research and Creative Activity Award from the Faculty of Community Services, Toronto Metropolitan University for her research projects which aim to centre Haudenosaunee worldviews and decolonize the profession of dietetics.

name: Salma Emara
title: Assistant Professor, Teaching Stream @ University of Toronto
bio: Salma Emara is an Assistant Professor, Teaching Stream in the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at the University of Toronto. She received her B.Sc. in Electronics and Communications Engineering from the American University in Cairo in 2018 and her Ph.D. in Computer Engineering from the University of Toronto under the supervision of Professor Baochun Li in 2022. Her Ph.D. research focused on improving reinforcement learning algorithms for computer networking. Currently, her research explores pedagogical strategies for enhancing debugging skills in beginner programmers and leveraging natural language processing in engineering education. She believes engineers learn best by doing and is committed to engaging students through in-class activities and problem-solving assignments. Her dedication to teaching has been recognized with multiple student-voted teaching awards.

name: Katharine Andrea Scott
title: Associate Professor @ University of Waterloo
bio: K. Andrea Scott specialized in fluid dynamics for her MASc and PhD degrees, studying acoustics and turbulence. Always passionate about the environment, she started working in a new area for postdoctoral research, on sea ice. Starting as a Postdoctoral Researcher with the Data Assimilation and Satellite Meteorology Research Section, Environment and Climate Change Canada, she was part of a team involved in the development of the Canadian sea ice data assimilation system. In 2012, she joined the Department of Systems Design Engineering, University of Waterloo, and began working on sea ice remote sensing using passive and active satellite-based microwave data. Given the complexity of sea ice signatures in these data, her team was one of the first to apply deep learning to this problem. Recently moving to the Department of Mechanical and Mechatronics Engineering, she now focuses on lake ice, sea ice and river ice, as well as a blend of physics-based and data-driven problems.
